title: Classic Romantic Fantasy Creator Returns With New Anime After 11 Years – Watch First Look Trailer
content:
The creator behind a classic romantic fantasy anime series is coming back with a new anime after 11 long years, and the first look has been revealed at what fans can expect from the new project. Julietta Suzuki has made waves with fans in all sorts of ways with a number of major releases over the years, but their arguably biggest work has been with Kamisama Kiss. But now Suzuki’s latest manga series has confirmed that it’s now working on its own anime adaptation next.

Julietta Suzuki’s Otaku Vampire’s Love Bite originally hit the pages of Hakusensha’s Hana to Yume magazine back in 2022 , and now it has been officially confirmed that the franchise will be making its jump to screens with a TV anime next. Licensed for an English language release with Viz Media, and to celebrate the new anime’s release, you can check out the first look trailer and teaser poster for Otaku Vampire’s Love Bite below.

Otaku Vampire’s Love Bite Announces New Anime

Otaku Vampire’s Love Bite has now confirmed it’s working on a new anime series, but unfortunately has not revealed much concrete information as to what to expect from its debut. No release window or date has been announced for the series as of this time, nor have any production staff, studio, or voice cast revealed. Outside of the fact that Viz Media has licensed the anime for an English language release when it hits in the future, there’s not much to go on for it at this time. But Viz Media is releasing the manga’s physical volumes.

As for what to expect from Otaku Vampire’s Love Bite , the series focuses on a vampire named Hina. She had spent decades as a shut-in before deciding to move to Japan in order to fully pursue her nerdy hobbies. When she meets her neighbor Kyuta, she discovers that he surprisingly looks just like her favorite character she often obsesses over. Making matters even more interesting is that Kyuta’s blood is irresistible to vampires, and all sorts of wacky shenanigans pop up when they start crowding around him. Given Kamisama Kiss ‘ own success , fans could hope to see the same here.

Will Otaku Vampire’s Love Bite Be an Anime Hit?

Otaku Vampire’s Love Bite could have the potential to be the next big thing when it hits. Kamisama Kiss remains one of the most popular anime from the 2010s even over a decade after its original release , and you can find it streaming on platforms like Crunchyroll and Netflix in the meantime. But it’s because it scratched a fantasy romance itch that fans couldn’t find elsewhere, and there’s a chance the same could be said here with this new series. Especially if it manages to tap into that same 2010s vibe that Julietta Suzuki’s other franchises have.

Vampire anime series are a dime a dozen, and many of them often have these romantic hooks at the center. But this one takes a different angle with its nerdy main character, and there’s a chance we’ll see all sorts of romantic misunderstandings and more when it hits. Are you curious about Otaku Vampire’s Love Bite ? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments!

title: Yayū Murata Launches Kickstarter for Across the Strange Edge Manga's 2nd Volume, Deluxe Hardcover Omnibus
content:
Yayū Murata announced on Wednesday a Kickstarter project to fund an English version of the second volume of his Across the Strange Edge ( Okashiki Sekai no Kyōkaisen ) series, along with a deluxe hardcover book including the first two volumes and a special cover designed in collaboration with Takashi Kumatani. The campaign will launch on November 19, and it will seek to raise €7,000 (about US$7,900) by December 17.

If funded, the books will get digital and physical releases in May 2027. There are two more deluxe hardcover volumes planned. Rewards for the new campaign include an original shikishi art board and art prints.

The project's page describes the story:

Misuzu has lived her life without ever knowing what a true “friend” is. After losing her mother at a young age and being raised by a father who was constantly busy, she grew up with little emotional expression and found it difficult to connect deeply with others. Her classmate Chizuru , bright and energetic by nature, is isolated for a different reason—she can see beings that do not belong to this world, a trait that makes people keep their distance. Their paths draw closer on the night of a summer festival, after an unsettling supernatural incident. When Misuzu is nearly tricked out of money by her classmates, Chizuru appears and delivers a warning from the spirit lingering behind Misuzu. From that strange encounter, the distance between the two girls begins to shrink. As they spend more time together, they slowly share the “worlds” they each live in, and within the brief span of that summer, they quietly—but unmistakably—form a bond that feels special. But the closer they become, the more they step toward a boundary they were never meant to cross. And soon, the two worlds they belong to begin quietly pulling them apart.

Murata originally launched the series as a one-shot for Shogakukan 's Manga ONE platform, where it won an award. The serialization began on the same platform in 2020. Shogakukan shipped the fifth and final compiled book volume in August 2021.

Murata ended the Unjō ni Utaite, Kimi wo Matsu ( I'm singing above the cloud, waiting for you. ) manga on March 6. Murata debuted the manga in July 2024. Houbunsha published the manga's the fifth volume on March 13.

title: Shonen Jump Confirms Release Date for Its Next Surprise Live-Action Movie
content:
Shueisha’s Weekly Shonen Jump magazine has surprisingly revealed their next major series going to the big screen with a new live-action movie, and has already confirmed its release date for a launch in Japan. Shonen Jump has seen a number of their long running franchises come to their respective ends, but at the same time those projects have also been returning for new adaptations. This includes a number of surprise live-action feature films, and the next one is already on the way for 2027.

Hajime Komoto’s Mashle: Magic and Muscles might have ended its original manga run a few years ago at this point , but the franchise has announced it’s coming back with a brand new live-action feature film release next year. Warner Bros. Japan is teaming up with a notable production studio behind other live-action anime and manga adaptations to take on the project, and has revealed the first look at the new Mashle live-action movie that you can check out below ahead of its launch in Japan next March.

Mashle: Magic and Muscles Live-Action Movie Announced for 2027

The new Mashle: Magic and Muscles live-action feature film will be hitting theaters across Japan on March 19th next year, but potential international release plans has yet to be announced as of this time. Warner Bros. and Fuji TV are overseeing the film with CREDEUS handling the production. This studio has been behind a number of successful manga and anime live-action adaptation franchises such as the Golden Kamuy films, Kingdom, Sakamoto Days, Under Ninja and more. So the studio has quite a bit of experience in this area.

TOHO will be overseeing the distribution for the new film’s release in Japan, but production staff and cast for the film have yet to be revealed as of this time. Mashle: Magic and Muscles is a hilarious new take for a live-action release as Warner Bros. is also gearing up for their next generation of the Harry Potter franchise too. The two franchises are often compared with one another for the way Mashle parodies magical school stories, so fans will be able to directly address the two adaptations soon enough.

When Does Mashle: Magic and Muscles Season 3 Come Out?

For those who are wanting more of the TV anime instead, thankfully Mashle: Magic and Muscles has also confirmed that the series is working on its third season with a release slated for the near future. While it has yet to confirm a concrete release date as of the time of this writing, MASHLE: MAGIC AND MUSCLES The Tri-Magicathlon Divine Visionary Final Exam Arc is scheduled to debut sometime next January as part of the Winter 2027 anime schedule.

The new season will be streaming with Crunchyroll when it finally hits , and that’s where you can catch up with everything that’s happened in the first two seasons in the meantime. Mashle: Magic and Muscles is a fun blend of action and comedy that takes down more serious magical school series down a peg, so it’s going to be interesting to see whether or not that translates as well into live-action as the anime and manga versions did. What do you think of Mashle going live-action next? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments!

title: Sugar Apple Fairy Tale's Miri Mikawa, Brave10's Kairi Shimotsuki Launch New Manga on November 24
content:
Shinchosha 's Kurage Bunch website announced on Friday that writer Miri Mikawa and artist Kairi Shimotsuki will launch a new manga titled Ryū no Kuni Gensō (Dragon Country Fantasy) on November 24.

The manga is set in Ryū no Hara (Dragon Plains), a realm that safeguards the slumber of dragons. Here, women who cannot hear the dragons' voices are despised as "Yūshi" or wanderers. But, men who can hear the dragons' voices are also detested. Hiori, whose older sister was killed as a "Yūshi," is bent on avenging her sister and rewriting the country's laws. To achieve her goals, she disguises herself as a man, heads to the imperial throne, marries Haruhana, the former emperor's daughter who also holds a great secret.

Mikawa and aki launched the original Sugar Apple Fairy Tale light novel series in April 2010, and ended it in the 17th volume in February 2015. The original novel series received a new collector's edition for the first three volumes, which shipped in December 2022, February 2023, and March 2023. Yen Press has licensed both the original light novel series and Yozora no Udon 's manga adaptation. The novel series inspired a two- cours (quarter of a year) anime in 2023.

Shimotsuki's Brave10 manga inspired a television anime in 2012, and Crunchyroll streamed the anime as it aired in Japan. NIS America released a Blu-ray Disc box of Brave10 in 2013.

Shimotsuki ended the Arthur Bright manga with its fourth volume, which shipped in June 2019. Shimotsuki launched the manga in Tokuma Shoten 's Comic Zenon magazine in May 2017.

Shimotsuki ended the Sabiiro no Armor: Reimei ( Rusted Armors: Dawn ) manga in May 2022. The manga launched in Kadokawa 's Monthly Comic Gene magazine in May 2021.

title: Sakamoto Holidays Manga Heads Towards Climax
content:
Tetsu Ōkawa reported on Saturday that the Sakamoto Holidays spinoff manga of Yuuto Suzuki 's Sakamoto Days manga is reaching its climax.

Viz Media publishes the series in English and describes the story:

Kill some time with former hit man Taro Sakamoto as he solves neighborhood crimes in this spinoff! Sakamoto, a former legendary assassin, runs a neighborhood store in the Ikoraizaka shopping arcade, but this street lined with various stores can be a little dangerous… To protect his beloved family and enjoy his days off, Sakamoto takes on the mission of revitalizing the area to make it the most peaceful shopping arcade in town! This hilarious spinoff of Sakamoto Days is now open to the public! Sakamoto and Shin catch a shoplifter, but the shoplifter returns with his gang to ambush them. Can Sakamoto and Shin defend themselves without spilling blood, keep Hana unaware of what's happening, and complete the housework perfectly?

Ōkawa launched the series in Shueisha 's Weekly Shonen Jump magazine in July 2024. Shueisha shipped the fourth compiled book volume on August 4. Viz Media shipped the second compiled volume on August 18.

Suzuki launched the original Sakamoto Days manga in Shueisha 's Weekly Shonen Jump magazine in November 2020. Shueisha published the 29th compiled book volume on November 4. Suzuki published a one-shot titled "Sakamoto" in Jump Giga in December 2019.

The original Sakamoto Days manga announced in July that it is heading to its climax. The manga started its "final battle" in August 2025. The series reached 18 million copies in circulation worldwide in August.

The first season of the original manga's anime adaptation premiered on TV Tokyo and affiliated channels on January 11, 2025, and the series also debuted on Netflix on that day. The first season's second part premiered in July 2025. The anime's second season will premiered in January 2027.

title: Reincarnation in the Game World Dan-Katsu Reveals New Trailer Featuring Additional Cast, Theme Songs
content:
Reincarnation in the Game World Dan-Katsu: Game Addict Plays “Encouragement for Job Hunting in Dungeons” From a “New Game” anime revealed a new trailer that features four additional cast members. The anime premieres in January 2027. Joining Yuto Uemura (the voice of the main character Zephyrus) in the cast are:

• Ayaka Nanase as Hanna

• Kotone Izumi as Sierra

• Hikaru Iida as Lana

• Chihaya Asakura as Ester

MindaRyn sings the opening theme song “Play the Play,” while LINKL PLANET performs the ending theme song “My Life Story.”

Studio Massket is animating the series with Nagisa Miyazaki as director. Yuji Kobayashi is handling the script and series composition. The anime is based on a light novel series written by Kaede Nishikigi and illustrated by Shuri. It was initially serialized online on Kakuyomu in January 2021. TO Books later acquired the title and has published 16 volumes in total. There is also a manga adaptation with art by Hiroshi Asagi that has been serialized online via TO Books’ Corona EX manga service since April 2022. Tobikawa is publishing the light novel series in French and English, describing the story as follows: Dan-Katsu is a legendary role-playing game that allows you to play more than 1021 classes and has more than 400 possible endings! The more we delve into it, the more we discover new ways to enjoy it, new objects… A certain gamer (player name: Zephyrus) is reincarnated in the world of Dan-Katsu, of which he becomes the main character. Overjoyed, he joins the Labyrinth Academy, the place where the main story takes place. He quickly obtains the ‘Hero’ class, the best in the game, but discovers that the ‘Muscle Warrior’, a class considered ‘for fun’ where he comes from, is perceived in this world as a good class?! That the most difficult dungeons have never been conquered?! In other words… he will be able to enjoy this world as if it were a new game! Determined to show everyone what a good class is, he brings together classmates, allows his reserved childhood friend to become an Alchemist, transforms a selfish Princess into a Saint… Now that he has gathered powerful classes around from him, he is ready to conquer the dungeons! Source: Reincarnation in the Game World Dan-Katsu anime Official website © Kaede Nishikigi, TO Books / Production Committee

title: Mashle: Magic and Muscles Live-Action Film Adaptation Announced
content:
Hajime Komoto’s Mashle: Magic and Muscles manga is officially getting a live-action film adaptation, with its Japanese theatrical premiere set for March 19, 2027.

A super teaser visual was released alongside the announcement, featuring protagonist Mash Burnedead from behind in his school robe while holding a dumbbell instead of a wand. The actor playing Mash is scheduled to be revealed on November 5.

Warner Bros. Pictures and Fuji Television are overseeing the production, with CREDEUS handling production and Toho distributing the film in Japan. CREDEUS has previously worked on live-action projects including Kingdom , Blue Lock and Kokuho .

Hajime Komoto writes and draws the Mashle manga, which has been serialized in Weekly Shonen Jump since January 2020. VIZ licensed it in English, and you can also read it on MANGA Plus. The platform describes the story as: This is a world of magic where magic is used for everything. But deep in the forest exists a young man who spends his time training and bulking up. He can’t use magic, but he enjoys a peaceful life with his father. But one day, his life is put in danger! Will his muscular body protect him from the magic users who are out to get him? Powerfully trained muscles crush magic as this abnormal magical fantasy begins!

The first season of Mashle: Magic and Muscles ended in June after running for 12 episodes. The second season also ran for 12 episodes in Winter 2024 and covered the Divine Visionary Selection Exam Arc . The next in the manga is the Tri-Magic-Athalon Divine Visionary Final Exam Arc , which is set to begin in January 2027 with Season 3 .

The voice cast for the Mashle anime adaptation includes:

• Chiaki Kobayashi as Mash Burnedead

• Kaito Ishikawa as Lance Crown

• Takuya Eguchi as Dot Barrett

• Reiji Kawashima as Finn Ames

• Reina Ueda as Lemon Irvine

• Yuki Kaji as Rayne Ames

• Yuichiro Umehara as Abel Walker

• Hiroki Nanami as Abyss Razor

title: 'Ramen Akeneko 2nd Season' Announces New Staff
content:
The official website for the television anime adaptation of Angyaman 's Ramen Akaneko ( Red Cat Ramen ) revealed new staff and key visual (pictured) for the upcoming second season . The anime is scheduled to premiere in January 2027 on Tokyo TV.

Staff Director: Hisatoshi Shimizu ( Taisou Zamurai ) Series Composition, Script: Shigeru Murakoshi ( Kaya-chan wa Kowakunai ) NEW Character design, Chief Animation Director: Michinori Chiba ( SK∞ ) Art Director: Julieta Colás ( Ousama Ranking: Yuuki no Takarabako ) NEW , Yann Le Gall ( Ninja Kamui ) 3D Supervisor: Tomohiko Suga ( Undead Girl Murder Farce ) Color Design: Chikako Kamata ( Jujutsu Kaisen ) Director of Photography: Shinichi Igarashi ( Hai to Gensou no Grimgar ) Editing: Keisuke Yanagi ( Tokyo Ghoul ), ACE NEW Sound Director: Akane Maeda ( Kaginado ) Sound Effects: Maki Takuma ( Jibaku Shounen Hanako-kun ) Music: Hirotaka Matsuoka ( Egg Car ) Studio: E&H Production Production: E&H Production, Good Smile Company

Note: The staff denoted with the legend NEW are new in their respective roles .

Produced by E&H Production, the first season aired in 12 episodes in Summer 2024. Crunchyroll streamed the series with English subtitles.

Angyaman originally submitted the manga as a webcomic on the Jump Rookie website in November 2021, where it ranked first. The manga then ran as an indie serialization for 29 chapters from March to October 2022 on the Shounen Jump+ web magazine and was promoted to an official serialization the following week. The 16th volume was released by Shueisha November 4th 2026.

title: Black Clover Season 2 Episode 6 Previews Noelle and Charlotte Facing Vanica
content:
Black Clover Season 2 has released preview images and synopsis for Episode 6 (Episode 176 overall) ahead of its November 7 premiere. The new season officially began on October 3, 2026 , with Crunchyroll streaming it worldwide. The anime previously revealed a special Devil Union Asta visual following Episode 3. The official Episode 6 “The Sacred Valkyrie” synopsis:

After an intense hand-to-hand battle, Magna emerged victorious against Dante!! With Dante defeated, only two members of the Dark Triad remain to be taken down in order to stop the advent of Qliphoth. One of them, Vanica, uses not only her own Blood Magic but also Curse-Warding Magic, a power granted by her devil, to control Lolopechka, whom she abducted from the Heart Kingdom, forcing her to attack Charlotte and Rill. Just then, Noelle and Gaja arrive on the scene. To counter the power of devils, Noelle has borrowed the power of the Water Spirit, Undine, and acquired a new form of magic known as “Saint Stage”!

You can see the preview images below:

The main staff for Season 2 includes:

• Director: Ayataka Tanemura

• Series Composition: Keiichiro Ochi

• Character Design: Itsuko Takeda

• Sub-Character Design: Kumiko Tokunaga

• Prop Design: Kosei Takahashi

• Music: Minako Seki

• Animation Production: Studio Pierrot

The opening song by WANIMA is titled “Kienai Riyuu” (The Reason That Won’t Disappear).

ALSO READ: Black Clover Creator Draws Toru Oikawa From Haikyu!! Black Clover Final Volume and Official Guidebook Released, Includes New 15-Page Manga by Yuki Tabata

You can also see the main visual .

The Black Clover manga was serialized in the Weekly Shonen Jump magazine from 2015 to August 2023, before transferring to Jump GIGA . It entered its final arc in August 2022 and officially ended on May 1 after eleven years of serialization. The manga is available to read on Viz Media’s website, MANGA Plus website, and the Shonen Jump mobile app in English.

It received a 170-episode anime adaptation by Studio Pierrot, which ran from 2017 to 2021. The Black Clover: Sword of the Wizard King movie premiered on June 16 and is streaming on Netflix. Crunchyroll streams the TV anime, and they describe the story:

In a world where magic is everything, Asta and Yuno are both found abandoned at a church on the same day. While Yuno is gifted with exceptional magical powers, Asta is the only one in this world without any. At the age of fifteen, both receive grimoires, magic books that amplify their holder’s magic. Asta’s is a rare Grimoire of Anti-Magic that negates and repels his opponent’s spells. Being opposite but good rivals, Yuno and Asta are ready for the hardest of challenges to achieve their common dream: to be the Wizard King. Giving up is never an option!

title: This Cult Sci-fi Movie Was Roasted by Critics 38 Years Ago, But It Changed Movies, Video Games, and Art Forever
content:
There are definitely movies that age badly. And there are films that look even better decades later. Then there’s the rare one that defies all expectations. Imagine a futuristic city filled with neon lights, motorcycle gangs, and enough government corruption to make everybody suspicious. Surprisingly, that’s still a concept that is hard to find in modern stories. Now add psychic teenagers and a military experiment that goes horribly wrong—things are about to get cooking.

Audiences in Japan got their first look at this bizarre science-fiction anime in 1988. American critics weren’t the most positive when it arrived from overseas. Some dismissed its story as confusing, while others weren’t particularly impressed by its relentless violence. The ironic thing is, plenty of filmmakers and artists saw something worth borrowing from. Its influence eventually reached Hollywood, video games, and music videos. Even people who have never watched an anime movie have probably encountered something that owes it a major debt.

Akira Was the Sci-Fi Movie American Critics Completely Misunderstood

Katsuhiro Otomo’s Akira arrived in Japanese theaters in July 1988. He adapted his own manga into a story about a futuristic Tokyo struggling to recover from disaster. The new city represents a chaotic mix of urban problems. Motorcycle gangs terrorize the streets. Politicians fight to maintain control, and the military conducts clandestine experiments that probably should have stayed behind closed doors. Two teenagers named Kaneda and Tetsuo find themselves caught up in the mix. Their new friendship takes a nasty turn when Tetsuo develops terrifying psychic abilities after being adducted and experimented on. Suddenly, the biggest threat to Neo-Tokyo isn’t another street gang. It’s a teenager who can barely control his own powers.

Early in my anime career, I watched Akira on VHS before I was old enough to fully understand it. I watched it several times, and beyond appreciating its animation and music, the characters and story truly stuck with me. The plot isn’t overly complicated; there are just so many layers to peel back and analyze. But that’s part of the movie’s appeal. I never finished buying and reading the entire manga series, but that’s going to change soon. This story is a masterpiece as both an anime and cinematic film. If you haven’t already, you need to experience this work of art.

The movie looks incredible. That’s probably the easiest way to describe it. Otomo created a futuristic city that feels crowded and alive. Its glowing advertisements and enormous buildings give Neo-Tokyo a personality of its own. The motorcycle sequences are still spectacular. The animation is packed with details that most movies wouldn’t bother attempting. More than 160,000 animation cels helped bring the film to life. American critics weren’t immediately impressed, though. When Akira reached American audiences in 1990, some reviewers found its story difficult to follow. The Los Angeles Times famously dismissed it as “High-Tech Hokum From Japan.” That’s a pretty brutal assessment for a movie that would eventually become a landmark of science-fiction storytelling.

How Akira Changed Hollywood Movies, Video Games, and Art Forever

You don’t have to look very hard to find Akira ‘s fingerprints on modern science fiction. The Wachowskis admired Japanese animation while developing The Matrix . The influence shows in the film’s futuristic atmosphere and its approach to visual storytelling. Other filmmakers followed similar paths. Even Stranger Things has played with imagery that recalls Otomo’s work. Then there’s Kanye West’s Stronger music video. Anyone familiar with Akira will recognize some of its most obvious references. It’s a little funny when you think about it. The Absolute Batman comic did an homage cover to the famous Kaneda poster. There are even rumors circulating about a live-action adaption . A Japanese animated film that confused American critics eventually became inspiration for some of Hollywood’s biggest creative projects.

Video games have embraced its world just as enthusiastically. Those towering buildings and glowing streets practically invite players to get lost in Neo-Tokyo. The motorcycle designs have become particularly recognizable, and artists still return to the movie for inspiration. You can find its influence in illustrations, fashion, and all sorts of digital artwork. But the biggest achievement might be what Akira did for animation itself. Otomo never treated the medium like something that needed to stay small or simple. He gave audiences a sprawling science-fiction epic with the ambition of a major Hollywood production. That’s another reason why the film is so important. It showed a generation of creators that animation could go almost anywhere. Critics eventually moved on to the next movie. Artists kept coming back to this one. And nearly four decades later, Neo-Tokyo still feels more alive than plenty of fictional cities that arrived long after it.
